Fine-mapping and the missing regulation

Why PGC3 schizophrenia loci fail to colocalize with brain eQTLs — a quantitative dissection

Author

Connor Finnerty (analysis pipeline: github-tracked, fully regenerable from public downloads)

Published

August 11, 2026

The question

Genome-wide significant schizophrenia loci overwhelmingly sit in non-coding sequence, yet they colocalize with brain expression QTLs far less often than a purely regulatory model predicts — the “missing regulation” puzzle. This report reproduces that observation on fully public data and quantitatively tests four competing explanations. Every number and figure regenerates from raw downloads via the project Snakefile; parameters live in config/config.yaml.

Data: PGC3 SCZ (Trubetskoy et al. 2022) primary autosome meta-analysis; 287 loci (Supplementary Table 3, SHA256-pinned) → 281 analysable (1 MHC, 5 chrX excluded). eQTLs: 13 GTEx v8 brain tissues + MetaBrain cortex-EUR (bulk), BrainSeq/ROSMAP/CommonMind DLPFC (power ladder), Walker 2019 fetal neocortex, Bryois 2022 sc-eQTLs (8 cell types). LD: 1000G GRCh38 EUR (n=503). All GRCh38, coloc 5.2.3 / susieR 0.14.2.

Stage 1 — the gap replicates

Dataset class Colocalized (PP4>0.8) Fraction Wilson 95% CI
0 GTEx cortex (N=205) 27/281 10% 7%–14%
1 MetaBrain cortex-EUR (N≈2,700) 55/281 20% 15%–25%
2 Any of 13 GTEx brain tissues 67/281 24% 19%–29%
3 Any of 14 bulk brain datasets 90/281 32% 27%–38%

Positive controls anchor the pipeline: FURIN at 15-rs4702 (PP4 = 0.99996, MetaBrain) and ZNF823 at its two chr19 loci top the colocalization list. Of the 191 non-colocalizing loci, 180 (94%) contain at least one gene with a brain eQTL at p < 1e-6 in the ±1 Mb window — regulation is present but tags different variants.

Stage 2 — four explanations, one ledger

Step Loci Cumulative
0 Stage 1 bulk colocalization 90 90

(a) Allelic heterogeneity — reshapes more than it enlarges

value
Loci with ≥2 GWAS credible sets 112/281
Multi-CS among misses vs hits 40% vs 39% (Fisher p=0.90)
Rescued (miss→hit) 23
Demoted (hit→signals separate) 23 of 85 abf hits

Multi-signal architecture is common everywhere (~40% of loci) but not enriched among misses — heterogeneity is not the primary explanation for the gap. Its real effect is churn: 27% of single-variant coloc hits dissolve when signals are fine-mapped and paired individually (e.g. 22-rs9607782 × ENSG00000232710: abf PP4 = 0.97 → PP3 = 0.98, peaks ~30 kb apart), while a similar number of misses are rescued (e.g. 8-rs4129585: 0.56 → 0.99). Single-causal-variant colocalization misclassifies roughly a quarter of calls in both directions.

(b) eQTL power — significant, saturating

Dataset eQTL N Fraction colocalized n
0 QTD000176 175 6% 16
1 QTD000051 479 11% 32
2 QTD000434 560 17% 48
3 QTD000075 586 16% 46
4 MetaBrain_Cortex_EUR 2683 20% 55

Logistic OR = 2.5 per 10× eQTL sample size (p = 3.8e-06), but the curve flattens: extrapolated bulk-cortex ceiling ≈ 25%. Power explains part of the gap; it cannot close it.

(c) Cell-type dilution — small now, clearly under-sampled

value
Loci colocalizing in ≥1 of 8 cell types (N=192!) 37
Missed by both bulk cortex datasets 13
Missed by all 14 bulk datasets 6

Per donor, sc-eQTLs are strikingly productive (37 loci at N=192 vs 16 for bulk DLPFC at N=175); excitatory neurons dominate (23), then oligodendrocytes (12). Given the power curve in (b), this is the explanation most likely to grow.

(d) Fetal / context specificity — weakest direct support, instructive twist

value
Fetal-eQTL colocalizations (N=211) 20
…among Stage-1 misses 5
CS fetal-regulatory PIP, hits vs misses 0.139 vs 0.085 (MWU p=0.001)
Fetal-not-adult enrichment OR=0.99, p=1.00

Contrary to the fetal-enhancer hypothesis, non-colocalizing loci show less credible-set overlap with fetal regulatory chromatin than colocalizing loci — and the depletion is even stronger for adult chromatin (0.048 vs 0.136). The unexplained loci are not hiding in fetal enhancers; their credible sets sit in sequence not annotated as regulatory in any surveyed brain context.

Threshold sensitivity

PP4 threshold GTEx cortex MetaBrain Any bulk brain coloc-SuSiE (6 ds) Any Bryois cell type
0 0.5 53 81 151 89 100
1 0.7 35 64 111 76 59
2 0.8 27 55 90 65 37
3 0.9 13 40 62 52 19

The qualitative picture — a majority of loci without eQTL support — is threshold-robust.

Ranked verdict

  1. eQTL power — strongest statistical signal, bounded upside (~25% ceiling).
  2. Single-variant-assumption error (allelic heterogeneity) — corrects ~26% of classifications in both directions; a methods lesson more than a gap-closer.
  3. Cell-type dilution — small measured contribution, largest growth potential.
  4. Fetal-specific regulation — minimal direct contribution; chromatin evidence redirects the hypothesis toward contexts not yet assayed.

57% of SCZ loci (159/281) resist all four explanations. Combined with the chromatin depletion result, the data favour regulation acting in unmeasured contexts (developmental windows, activity-dependent states, rare cell populations) or non-eQTL mechanisms (splicing, APA, protein-level) as the residual explanation — matching and extending the published missing-regulation argument.

Extension: splicing, methylation, and robustness

Channel Newly explained Total hits (PP4>0.8)
0 bulk_expression 90 90
1 susie_rescue 23 23
2 single_cell 6 37
3 fetal_eqtl 4 20
4 splicing 9 47
5 methylation 84 193
6 UNEXPLAINED 65

Extending the ledger to two further molecular layers changes the verdict qualitatively. Splicing (17 brain sQTL datasets): 47 loci colocalize, 9 of them surviving every prior channel. Methylation (Brain-mMeta, ~1,160 brains): 193/281 loci share a causal variant with a brain CpG, including 118 of the 191 expression-orphan loci — collapsing the unexplained core from 57% to 23% (65 loci). This is not a trait-multiplicity artifact: per-test colocalization runs ~6× higher for methylation than expression (1.2% vs 0.2%) at comparable test counts per locus, and 68 expression-misses persist even at PP4 > 0.95.

Interpretation: most “missing regulation” loci are demonstrably epigenetically active in adult brain — the shared causal variant moves DNA methylation — while the transcriptional consequence stays invisible to every surveyed eQTL context. Colocalization is mechanism-symmetric (methylation need not mediate risk), but combined with the credible-set chromatin depletion, the coherent reading is regulation whose expression effects are context-, state-, or timing-restricted, or buffered at steady state.

Robustness: EUR-only GWAS reruns agree with the primary analysis at 94–96% of classifications (Spearman PP4 ≈ 0.89); LD-mismatch diagnostics (kriging_rss) show a median 2% outlier fraction with no locus above 5%; fetal-mQTL overlap is depleted among expression misses (OR 0.30, p = 6e-4), echoing the chromatin-depletion result.

Limitations

  1. Reference-panel LD (1000G n=503 vs N≈161k GWAS) limits GWAS-side SuSiE; 33 loci yield no credible set and 2 don’t converge. PolyFun with UKB LD is the designated sensitivity arm.
  2. eQTL-side SuSiE coverage is partial (six datasets with published lbf; small-N tissues often lack credible sets), making rescues conservative and demotions dataset-limited.
  3. MetaBrain public release lacks allele frequencies (GWAS-control MAF used for prior scaling) and its betas are Z-derived; Bryois ships no SEs (p-value route, fixed N=192).
  4. GWAS is EUR+EAS “primary” vs European eQTL panels; EUR-only GWAS sensitivity is queued.
  5. Expression-level only: splicing/isoform QTLs (PsychENCODE isoQTL, GTEx sQTL) not yet incorporated — a known additional explanation channel.
  6. context_score is a heuristic ranking for follow-up prioritization, not a calibrated posterior.

Reproducibility

git clone → conda env create -f envs/scz-coloc.yml → snakemake -s workflow/Snakefile all results/stage2/explanations.tsv results/stage2/fig_stage2.png --cores N --resources net=8 → quarto render report/report.qmd. Raw-data provenance (URLs, sizes, SHA256s) recorded in sidecar files at download time; the supplementary-table zip is checksum-pinned in config.
